'''Shlomo Magdassi''' is an Israeli [[chemist]] and professor at the Institute of Chemistry, Casali Center for Applied Chemistry, at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. He is known for his research in [[colloid]] and [[interface science]], [[nanomaterial]]s, and functional printing technologies, including [[printed electronics]] and [[3D printing|3D]] and [[4D printing]]. He is a Fellow of the [[National Academy of Inventors]].

== Early life and education ==
Magdassi was born in [[Ramla]], Israel. He studied chemistry and applied chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], receiving a BSc in 1978, an MSc in 1980, and a PhD in 1983 under the supervision of Nissim Garti.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ph.d Students {{!}} Prof. Nissim Garti |url=https://nissimgarti.huji.ac.il/people/teaching/phd-students |website=Institute of Chemistry |language=en}}</ref> He completed postdoctoral research at [[Ohio State University]] from 1984 to 1985 with Sylvan G. Frank.<ref name="huji-profile">{{cite web |title=Prof. Shlomo Magdassi |url=https://magdassi.huji.ac.il/prof-shlomo-magdassi |website=Hebrew University of Jerusalem}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Magdassi has spent his academic career at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where he joined the Institute of Chemistry as a lecturer in applied chemistry in 1986 and was promoted to professor in 2005.<ref name="huji-profile" />

Since 2021, he has headed the Casali Foundation, and in 2024 he was appointed Vice Dean for Entrepreneurship and Industry. He holds the Enrique Berman Chair in Solar Energy.<ref name="huji-profile" /> He was also the founder of the 3D and Functional Printing Center and served as chairman of ASPER-HUJI Innovate from 2019 to 2024.<ref name="huji-profile" />

He has served on the editorial boards of several scientific journals, including ''ACS Materials Letters'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Editors & Editorial Board |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/amlcef/editors.html |website=Acs.org}}</ref> ''Advanced Materials Technologies'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Advisory Board |url=https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/2365709x/2767_edbd.html |publisher=Wiley}}</ref> ''[[Virtual and Physical Prototyping]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Virtual and Physical Prototyping |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/nvpp20/about-this-journal#editorial-board |website=Taylor & Francis Online}}</ref> ''Colloid Journal'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Colloid Journal |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10595/editorial-board |website=SpringerLink |language=en}}</ref> and ''[[Coatings (journal)|Coatings]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/coatings/editors?page_no=9 |publisher=Mdpi.com}}</ref>

== Research ==
Magdassi’s research is in [[materials science]] and [[chemistry]], including micro- and [[nanomaterial]]s, [[colloid]] and [[interface science]], and functional materials. His work has included studies of [[dispersion (chemistry)|dispersions]], [[emulsion]]s, and related colloidal systems.

One area of his research concerns functional inks and materials for [[digital printing]] and [[printed electronics]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Farraj |first1=Yousef |last2=Kanner |first2=Aviad |last3=Magdassi |first3=Shlomo |title=E-Textile by Printing an All-through Penetrating Copper Complex Ink |journal=ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces |date=3 May 2023 |volume=15 |issue=17 |pages=21651–21658 |doi=10.1021/acsami.3c02242}}</ref> His work has included [[inkjet printing|inkjet-based]] fabrication methods and conductive inks based on [[metal]]lic [[nanoparticle]]s and other nanostructured materials, with applications in [[flexible electronics]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zarek |first1=Matt |last2=Layani |first2=Michael |last3=Cooperstein |first3=Ido |last4=Sachyani |first4=Ela |last5=Cohn |first5=Daniel |last6=Magdassi |first6=Shlomo |title=3D Printing of Shape Memory Polymers for Flexible Electronic Devices |journal=Advanced Materials (Deerfield Beach, Fla.) |date=June 2016 |volume=28 |issue=22 |pages=4449–4454 |doi=10.1002/adma.201503132 |url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26402320/ |issn=1521-4095}}</ref> [[sensor]]s,<ref>{{cite web |title=3D printing nanoresonators: Towards miniaturized and multifunctional sensors |url=https://phys.org/news/2021-11-3d-nanoresonators-miniaturized-multifunctional-sensors.html |publisher=Phys.org}}</ref> and [[energy]]-related devices.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kamyshny |first1=Alexander |last2=Sowade |first2=Enrico |last3=Magdassi |first3=Shlomo |title=Inkjet Ink Formulations: Overview and Fundamentals |journal=Inkjet Printing in Industry |date=16 August 2022 |pages=93–124 |doi=10.1002/9783527828074.ch5 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/0471238961.inkjmagd.a01 |publisher=Wiley |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Magdassi has also worked on materials for [[3D printing]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Surkes |first1=Sue |title=Israeli researchers make breakthrough in glass 3D printing |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/israeli-researchers-make-breakthrough-in-glass-3d-printing/ |website=The Times of Israel |date=30 September 2025}}</ref> and [[4D printing]], including [[polymer]] and composite systems with responsive properties.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Levin |first1=Ido |last2=Sachyani |first2=Ela |last3=Lieberman |first3=Rama |last4=Trink |first4=Noa |last5=Sharon |first5=Eran |last6=Magdassi |first6=Shlomo |title=4D printing of fully programmable sheets of digital metamaterials |journal=Soft Matter |date=6 March 2026 |doi=10.1039/D5SM00780A |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2026/sm/d5sm00780a |language=en |issn=1744-6848|doi-access=free }}</ref> Related work has involved printable systems that incorporate nanomaterials for functional or adaptive structures.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Solomon |first1=Shoshanna |title=Hebrew U team develops shape-shifting 3D printed pills for better targeted drugs |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/hebrew-u-team-develops-shape-shifting-3d-printed-pills-for-better-targeted-drugs/ |website=The Times of Israel |date=6 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Langnau |first1=Leslie |title=3D printing in water opens opportunities in medical research |url=https://www.engineering.com/3d-printing-water-opens-opportunities-medical-research/ |website=Engineering.com |date=3 August 2017}}</ref>

His research has also addressed nanomaterials in [[drug delivery]] and related delivery systems, including applications in [[cosmetics]] and [[pharmaceutical]]s, with work on [[controlled release]] and targeted delivery mechanisms.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Magdassi |first1=Shlomo |title=Delivery systems in cosmetics |journal=Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects |date=15 May 1997 |volume=123-124 |pages=671–679 |doi=10.1016/S0927-7757(97)03792-8 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0927775797037928 |issn=0927-7757|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Some of his research has been connected to industrial applications in areas such as digital printing, [[solar energy]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Colour-tuneable perovskite solar cell is 3D printed |url=https://www.iom3.org/resource/colour-tuneable-perovskite-solar-cell-is-3d-printed.html |website=Iom3.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Fleisher |first1=Jessica |title=New, Flexible Solar Cell That Works on Windows and Flexible Surfaces Developed by Hebrew University Nanotechnology Researchers |url=https://www.afhu.org/2026/01/12/new-flexible-solar-cell-that-works-on-windows-and-flexible-surfaces-developed-by-hebrew-university-nanotechnology-researchers/ |website=American Friends of the Hebrew University |date=12 January 2026}}</ref> [[electronics]], and consumer products,<ref>{{cite news |title=Ten discoveries that shaped the year {{!}} The Times of Israel |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/spotlight/ten-discoveries-that-shaped-the-year/ |work=The Times of Israel |date=11 January 2026}}</ref> including through collaborations and [[technology transfer]] activities.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Shamah |first1=David |title=After giant glass printers and printed lattés, Hebrew U seeks more 3D innovation |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/after-giant-glass-printers-and-printed-lattes-hebrew-u-seeks-more-3d-innovation/ |work=The Times of Israel |date=28 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Solomon |first1=Shoshanna |title=Nano-engineered pomegranate oil holds hope for brain disease, study shows |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/nano-engineered-pomegranate-oil-holds-hope-for-brain-disease-study-shows/ |work=The Times of Israel |date=23 June 2020}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* 2016 – Solvay Award, European Colloid and Interface Society<ref>{{cite web |title=ECIS-Syensqo Award |url=https://www.ecis-web.eu/awards/ecis-solvay-award/ |website=ECIS}}</ref>
* 2021 – Fellow of the [[National Academy of Inventors]]<ref>{{cite web |title=CLASS OF 2021 FELLOWS INDUCTION |url=https://academyofinventors.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Fellows-Program-5.20.22.pdf |publisher=National Academy of Inventors}}</ref>
* 2022 – Johann Gutenberg Prize, [[Society for Imaging Science and Technology]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Johann Gutenberg Prize |url=https://www.imaging.org/IST/IST/Membership/Awards/Johann_Gutenberg_Prize.aspx |website=Society for Imaging Science and Technology |language=en}}</ref>
* 2022 – Prize for Outstanding Scientist, Israel Chemical Society<ref>{{cite web |title=The ICS Prize for Outstanding Scientist|url=https://www.chemistry.org.il/prizes-page/?data=8 |publisher=Israel Chemical Society}}</ref>
* 2024 – Landau Prize for Arts and Sciences of [[Mifal HaPais]], in materials science and engineering.<ref>{{cite web |title=פרופ' שלמה מגדסי |url=https://culture.pais.co.il/landau_default/year/2024/magedsi_shlomo/ |website=מועצת הפיס לתרבות ולאמנות |publisher=מפעל הפיס |language=he}}</ref>
